results.title: Classification of moduli for which the Lucas numbers attain every residue
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every integer $m > 1$, with $L_n$ the Lucas numbers, every residue modulo $m$ is attained (for every $r$ with $0 \le r < m$ there is $n \ge 0$ with $L_n \equiv r \pmod m$) if and only if $m \in \{2, 4, 6, 7, 14\}$ or $m = 3^k$ for some integer $k \ge 1$.

results.title: Avila–Chen theorem on Lucas numbers modulo $m$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L_n$ denote the Lucas numbers. For every integer $m > 1$, every residue modulo $m$ is attained by the Lucas numbers (for every $r$ with $0 \le r < m$ there is $n \ge 0$ with $L_n \equiv r \pmod m$) if and only if $m \in \{2, 4, 6, 7, 14\}$ or $m = 3^k$ for some integer $k \ge 1$.

results.title: Absolute retract
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A topological space $K$ is an absolute retract when $K$ is compact and, for every separable metrizable space $X$ and every topological embedding $e \colon K \to X$, there is a continuous map $r \colon X \to K$ with $r(e(k)) = k$ for all $k \in K$.

results.title: Wilson convexity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subset $K$ of a pseudometric space $X$ with distance $d$ is convex in the sense of Wilson when for all $x, y \in K$ and every real $t$ with $0 \le t \le 1$ there is exactly one $z \in K$ with $d(x, z) = t \, d(x, y)$ and $d(z, y) = (1 - t) \, d(x, y)$.

results.title: Eilenberg's theorem on compact convex absolute retracts
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Compact operators are norm limits of finite-rank operators

results.title: Number of fixed tilings
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ (the cells) and $T$ (the tile designs) be finite sets, let $\varphi : \alpha \to \alpha$ be a map and let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $T$. The number of tilings fixed by $(\varphi, \sigma)$ is the number of maps $F : \alpha \to T$ such that $F(\varphi(c)) = \sigma(F(c))$ for every $c \in \alpha$.

results.title: Tile designs fixed by a power of a permutation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $T$ of tile designs, a permutation $\sigma$ of $T$ and a natural number $k$, this is the number of designs $d \in T$ with $\sigma^k(d) = d$.

results.title: Orbit of a cell under a permutation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set, $\varphi$ a permutation of $\alpha$ and $c \in \alpha$. The orbit of $c$ under $\varphi$ is the finite set $\{\varphi^k(c) : k \in \mathbb{N}\}$ of images of $c$ under the nonnegative powers of $\varphi$. Since $\alpha$ is finite, this is the orbit of $c$ under the cyclic group generated by $\varphi$.

results.title: Orbits of a permutation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set and $\varphi$ a permutation of $\alpha$. For $c \in \alpha$ let $O(c) = \{\varphi^k(c) : k \in \mathbb{N}\}$ be the orbit of $c$ under $\varphi$. The set of orbits of $\varphi$ is the set $\{O(c) : c \in \alpha\}$ of subsets of $\alpha$, in which each orbit occurs once.

results.title: Cylinder fixed-tiling count for the identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a finite set of tile designs, let $n, m \ge 1$, and let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $T$ with $\sigma^1 = 1$, that is, the identity. Then the cylinder shift sum of the identity map of $\mathbb{Z}/n \times \mathbb{Z}/m$ and $\sigma$ equals $\sum_{d \mid n} \varphi(d)\, |T|^{nm/d}$, where $d$ runs over the positive divisors of $n$ and $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function.

results.title: Linear extensions of a finite poset
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite poset with $n$ elements. Its linear extensions are represented as rank functions: the set of linear extensions of $\alpha$ is the finite set of all maps $\sigma : \alpha \to \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ that are bijective and monotone, meaning that $x \le y$ implies $\sigma(x) \le \sigma(y)$.

results.title: Membership in the linear extensions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite poset with $n$ elements. A map $\sigma : \alpha \to \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ belongs to the set of linear extensions of $\alpha$ if and only if $\sigma$ is bijective and monotone.

results.title: Ranking a Szpilrajn linear extension
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite poset with $n$ elements, and fix a linear order on $\alpha$ extending its partial order (one exists by Szpilrajn's extension theorem; it is chosen once and for all). This is the order isomorphism from $\alpha$ with that linear order onto $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ with its usual order.

results.title: A chosen linear extension
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite poset with $n$ elements, and fix a linear order on $\alpha$ extending its partial order (one exists by Szpilrajn's extension theorem; it is chosen once and for all). The chosen linear extension of $\alpha$ is the rank function $\alpha \to \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ sending each element to its position in that linear order, counted from $0$.

results.title: The chosen linear extension is bijective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite poset $\alpha$ with $n$ elements, the chosen linear extension of $\alpha$, viewed as a rank function $\alpha \to \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, is a bijection.

results.title: The chosen linear extension is monotone
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite poset $\alpha$ with $n$ elements, the chosen linear extension of $\alpha$, viewed as a rank function $\sigma : \alpha \to \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, is monotone: $x \le y$ implies $\sigma(x) \le \sigma(y)$.

results.title: Existence of linear extensions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every finite poset has a linear extension.

results.title: The number of linear extensions is positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite poset $\alpha$, the number of linear extensions of $\alpha$ is positive.

results.title: Maximal elements of a finite set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite subset $A$ of a partially ordered set $P$, the maximal elements of $A$ form the subset of those $x \in A$ such that every $y \in A$ with $x \le y$ equals $x$.

results.title: Membership in the maximal elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a finite subset of a partially ordered set $P$ and let $x \in P$. Then $x$ belongs to the set of maximal elements of $A$ if and only if $x \in A$ and every $y \in A$ with $x \le y$ equals $x$.

results.title: Correctness of quicksort
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $\ell$ over a linear order, the output of quicksort on $\ell$ is sorted in nondecreasing order and is a permutation of $\ell$; in particular every value occurs in the output exactly as often as in $\ell$.

results.title: Worst-case comparison bound for quicksort
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list of length $n$ over a linear order, quicksort performs at most $n(n-1)/2$ comparisons.
